question: Does the modest conditional city-area skill of the existing reference-population feature survive a contiguous-region test and separation of training/test hinterlands?
reason: The grain feature experiment is complete and negative relative to existing H. Do not tune grain or hours. Existing province-hash folds are noncontiguous; this test changes evaluation geometry only.
target: Same exposed664-record area development cohort, fixed AD200-compatible/inhabited-basis/known-end evaluation masks. Occupation intervals do not date extents. No new blind data or demographic calibration.
features: ONLY intercept-only M0 and intercept+log existing hinterland reference people H. Use exact sealed conditional_grain_extent features and supplied site geometry. No area-derived density/workforce feature, capital/hierarchy terms, grain models, new environmental solve or parameter search.
groups: For each source row use its supplied centre CELL latitude/longitude, not a separately rounded individual site position. Four fixed contiguous quadrants split at longitude17E and latitude38N: SW=(lat<38,lon<17), SE=(lat<38,lon>=17), NW=(lat>=38,lon<17), NE=(lat>=38,lon>=17). Boundary equality goes north/east. Rows sharing a centre always share a group. These are geometric regions, not historical provinces.
buffer: Distances in the SAME 9km projected grid plane as the 60km hinterlands. Outer test=one entire quadrant. Outer training=other quadrants AND minimum centre distance to ANY outer-test row centre strictly greater than120km. This excludes touching/overlapping 60km catchment disks across train/test. Still all known sites condition the common partition. No claim that 120 projected km is an exact geodesic distance.
inner: On each outer-training set, hold out each of its three remaining quadrant groups in turn. Inner training must also be strictly farther than120 projected km from every inner-test centre. Inner test is the matching quadrant subset of the fixed outer-training set. Fit least-squares mean using inner-training rows only; sigma is RMS of all inner-held-out log residuals. Outer mean is refitted on its fixed outer-training set. Both models use identical masks/buffers. No test outcomes in coefficients or sigma.
failure: Every inner/outer training set must contain at least10 rows and full design rank; each inner test nonempty. If geometry fails this gate, preserve an explicit no-fit closure without moving boundaries, shrinking buffer or changing cohorts. Empty evaluation-mask/group combinations retain n=0 and null scores.
scoring: 256 paired seeds1000..1255, same truncated-normal draws and inherited area bounds as preceding benchmark. Conditional log-area CRPS, median log MAE/RMSE/bias, generated-total/reference ratio for all664, AD200-compatible, strict and known-end masks; per-quadrant and pooled. Compare ONLY these newly fitted two models; archived scores are context, not paired comparisons under this changed training protocol. No significance/adoption cutoff chosen after results.
checks: Plan committed before geometry/fits. Verify sealed grain inputs and latest full protected inventory. Independently reconstruct groups/shared-centre identity and all buffer masks/distances; scalar-centred OLS and inner residual sigma; held-out outcome perturbation; direct pairwise CRPS and table checks; paired seeds, fresh byte-exact rerun and visual inspection of group/score diagnostic.
interpretation: This is a stricter exposed-development transfer diagnostic, not genuinely new validation. Region effects, mixed extent definitions and undated phases remain. A negative result blocks claims that the small old H gain transfers across these regions; a positive result does not establish historical household/draft resources or unlock atlas adoption.
output: Frozen group/support masks, fit receipts, ensembles, pooled/group score tables and one scientific map/score diagnostic with concise report. No all-data deployment fit, default change or published atlas update.
reserved_pools_and_climate: Remain closed/deferred. No reaping/plough evidence search.
